data.body:
Landed and closed.

Merged as `e6c03f1ede960b338161b13ab56eac6b35b42e67` via Gerrit change 3134 — 4 files, 26 insertions, 26 deletions, tests only. Both gates green on patch set 1 (`LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, 0 unresolved); `mergeable: true` confirmed before a revision-scoped submit.

Gerrit rebased this one on submit, so the merged SHA (`e6c03f1ede9`) differs from the pushed SHA (`5f874f6a49a`) — the EVAL slice had merged in between. The worktree was advanced to the merged commit before closing, and the ticket closed with `--ref e6c03f1ede960b338161b13ab56eac6b35b42e67`; all 7 ACs ticked.

The server-side rebase was clean and needed no intervention, unlike the two release-notes-touching slices. That is the practical payoff of this slice carrying no `docs/release-notes.md` entry: it was the only one of the three that could be pushed concurrently and submitted without an author rebase.

**This close unblocked the ENGINE slice.** The transition reported `unblocked: 43bd-2668-aa3e-4950`. `43bd` was blocked by all three of `ce4f`, `1969`, and `8c31`; with this close the last blocker is gone and ENGINE is now claimable.

Epic `87d8` slice status: AGG (`742d`), WORKFLOWS (`1969`), EVAL (`ce4f`), and REPOINT (`8c31`) are all merged and closed. ENGINE (`43bd`) is next, and its line citations are being re-measured against `e6c03f1ede9` before plan review — three of the four landed slices edited files ENGINE cites, so the citations recorded at `f8ddcaf88e6` cannot be assumed current.
